confidence_basis: Main PDF, OpenDataLoader output, fallback pypdf extraction, rendered methods pages, Nature HTML, and cited-protocol lineage to Canzoneri et al. 2012 were reviewed. The paper directly reports the four body-relative direction blocks, pink-noise motion, speaker geometry, gain range, tactile timings, condition rows, repetitions, catch trials, block count, and total trial count. Remaining uncertainty is mainly exact pink-noise file/seed, ITI distribution, and response timeout.

profile_recreation_assessment.reason: The study is a strong runnable four-direction trunk PPS profile: two physical speakers synthesize approaching/receding pink-noise motion in front, rear, left, and right blocks, with explicit tactile timings and per-row counts. Lab recreation still needs an approximate pink-noise source and a chosen ITI/response timeout because those are not numerically reported.

source_checks.scope: Reviewed overview, results timing description, methods page, Fig. 5, conditions, procedure, and data-availability section for Segment 1-4 values.
Used as primary extraction map for methods and timing/count rows, then checked against fallback extraction and rendered page images.
Searched all 10 pages for stimulus, audio, tactile, temporal delay, catch, randomized, block, trial, response, ITI, and supplement terms.
Temporary rendered pages were visually checked to verify timing rows, speaker layout, direction blocks, condition counts, and randomized procedure.
Nature HTML was checked for supplementary-information links and methods details; no supplement listing was exposed, and all Segment 1-4 values came from the main article.
Matsuda states it adopted the Canzoneri 2012 audio-tactile PPS task; Canzoneri was checked as the base dynamic-audio protocol lineage.

review_attempts.result: Captured the methods page with pink noise, speaker geometry, gain, tactile timing rows, condition percentages, counts, breaks, and randomization.
Confirmed page 7 as the main source for apparatus and count fields and page 2 as the overview/timing source.
Verified Fig. 5 and methods text for IN/OUT gradients, 10/110 cm speaker layout, four direction orientations, and condition counts.
Separated T1-T5 bimodal SOAs from Tbefore/Tafter unimodal baseline-like timings and confirmed that ITI was not numerically reported.
Mapped 100 bimodal, 40 unimodal, and 60 catch trials per direction block, with 4 blocks and 800 total trials.
Nature HTML exposed no supplement listing; the paper cites Canzoneri 2012 as the base task, and the current Matsuda paper supplies its own four-direction implementation details.

stimulus_type.value: Moving auditory stimuli were generated from 44.1 kHz pink noise.
stimulus_type.evidence_note: The methods identify the sound class and sample rate.

source_provenance.value: The paper says the audio stimuli were created from pink noise; exact source file, seed, or stimulus script is not supplied.
source_provenance.page_or_section: PDF p.7, Audio stimuli; Nature data availability
source_provenance.evidence_note: Stimulus provenance is reported at the class level, but no reusable asset is linked.

trajectory_count.value: Eight auditory motion trajectories: approaching and receding motion in each of four body-relative directions.
trajectory_count.evidence_note: The design crosses two audio motions with front, rear, left, and right direction blocks.

trajectory_path.value: Motion was synthesized between a near speaker 10 cm from the participant and a far speaker 110 cm away, with participants reoriented for front, rear, left, and right blocks.
trajectory_path.page_or_section: PDF p.7, Fig. 5 and Audio stimuli
trajectory_path.evidence_note: Speaker distances and direction-block orientations are shown and described.

stimulus_duration.evidence_note: The duration is directly reported for both approaching and receding sounds.

stimulus_speed.value: Pink-noise motion was linear and uniform at 33.3 cm/s between 10 and 110 cm.
stimulus_speed.evidence_note: Speed and spatial endpoints are explicitly reported.

auditory_conditions.value: Approaching and receding auditory motion conditions were tested in front, rear, left, and right body-relative directions.
auditory_conditions.evidence_note: The article describes the two audio motions and four direction blocks.

gain_envelope.value: Sound pressure changed exponentially over 55-70 dBA, increasing for approaching and decreasing for receding motion.
gain_envelope.evidence_note: The SPL range and direction of the envelope are reported.

renderer_or_apparatus.value: Unity 5.6.1f1 controlled the sequence; two JBL Control 1 Pro loudspeakers at sternum height presented the moving sound.
renderer_or_apparatus.evidence_note: Software and speaker model/placement are reported.

trial_rows_families.value: Each direction block contained bimodal audio-tactile trials, unimodal tactile-only timing trials, and no-tactile catch trials.
trial_rows_families.evidence_note: The three trial families are listed in the conditions section.

condition_intermixing.value: Trials from the three families and timing/motion cells were randomized within each direction block.
condition_intermixing.evidence_note: The procedure reports randomized trial order within each block.

blocked_or_random_order.value: Four body-relative direction blocks were used; block order was counterbalanced across participants.
blocked_or_random_order.evidence_note: Direction was blocked, while block order was counterbalanced.

iti_jitter_policy.page_or_section: PDF p.7 methods; Nature HTML checked 2026-06-16
iti_jitter_policy.evidence_note: No ITI, inter-trial interval, or jitter value/distribution was found after main PDF, fallback, visual, and publisher-route checks.

response_window.evidence_note: Participants responded quickly; RTs outside 100-1300 ms were excluded analytically, but no response timeout was reported.

task_sequence_rules.value: Participants were blindfolded, detected chest vibration regardless of sound, and withheld responses when no tactile stimulus occurred.
task_sequence_rules.evidence_note: Task instructions and catch-trial response rule are reported.

tactile_stimulus.value: A Nidec LD14-002 linear vibration actuator controlled by Arduino UNO delivered a 24 ms vibration on the chest.
tactile_stimulus.evidence_note: Tactile device, control hardware, site, and duration are reported.

soa_table.value: T1-T5 occurred 300, 800, 1500, 2200, and 2700 ms from sound onset; Tbefore was 700 ms before sound onset and Tafter was 700 ms after sound offset.
soa_table.evidence_note: All seven tactile timing values are directly reported.

baseline_strategy.value: Unimodal tactile-only trials used Tbefore and Tafter timings as pre/post-sound baseline-like controls without audio.
baseline_strategy.evidence_note: The unimodal family is explicitly defined as tactile stimulus without audio stimulus.

baseline_timing.value: Baseline-like tactile-only timings were Tbefore at -700 ms relative to sound onset and Tafter at +700 ms after sound offset.
baseline_timing.evidence_note: The same Tbefore/Tafter values define the unimodal timing rows.

catch_trial_type.value: Catch trials contained the sound sequence but no tactile stimulus; participants were instructed not to respond.
catch_trial_type.evidence_note: Catch trials were included to limit tactile-timing prediction.

repetitions_per_tactile_soa_condition.value: Per direction block, bimodal trials were 2 audio motions x 5 T1-T5 delays x 10 repetitions, giving 10 repetitions per motion-delay cell.
repetitions_per_tactile_soa_condition.evidence_note: The repetition formula is explicitly reported.

baseline_count.value: Each direction block had 40 unimodal tactile-only trials: 2 audio-motion timing labels x Tbefore/Tafter x 10 repetitions.
baseline_count.evidence_note: Unimodal baseline-like trial count and formula are reported.

catch_count.value: Each direction block had 60 no-tactile catch trials.

block_count.value: The experiment had four blocks, one each for front, rear, left, and right body-relative directions.
block_count.evidence_note: The direction-block structure is explicitly reported.

total_trial_count.value: Each block had 200 trials, for 800 total trials across four direction blocks.
total_trial_count.evidence_note: Per-block and total trial counts are reported.

critical_caveats: Exact pink-noise source file, random seed, and Unity implementation script are not supplied.
No ITI or jitter distribution was found.
No explicit response timeout is reported; only analysis exclusion cutoffs of 100-1300 ms are described.
Four directions were blocked by rotating participant orientation relative to the same two-speaker layout, not intermixed trial-by-trial.
Publisher HTML exposed no supplement listing; the automated supplement ledger previously had an HTTP 429 status rather than an actual downloaded supplement.
next_manual_action: Use this as a high-confidence four-direction dynamic trunk PPS profile. Implement ITI and response timeout as explicit lab-default approximations unless a later source or author-provided data/script reveals them.
